summary: Python 3.13 introduced an experimental just-in-time (JIT) compiler, built on the copy-and-patch approach, which can yield significant speedups for certain workloads. The Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled in the free-threaded build, enabling true parallelism for CPU-bound threads. The interactive interpreter (REPL) was redesigned with syntax highlighting, better multiline support, and improved history. An incremental garbage collector reduced GC pause times. Support policy changed: 3.13 and later receive two years of full support followed by three years of security support. The experimental JIT is opt-in and continues Python's 'Faster CPython' trajectory.
notes: Full bug-fix support until 2026-10-01; then security-only until 2029-10-31. The free-threaded build (python3.13t) is separate from the default build; adoption of free-threading is gradual. The JIT remains experimental and may evolve in 3.14 and beyond.
